title: ISS module and sleep station sound levels (2022 to 2024 surveys) and crew-worn noise dosimetry (2020, Increments 51 to 64)

instrument: Sound level meter surveys (spatial averages per module, sleep station interiors) and crew-worn acoustic dosimeters

segment.description: US or RS (Russian Segment) where stated

location.description: Module, sleep station or crew group

location_kind.description: work area, stowage, sleep station, crew-worn dosimeter

measured.description: Date of the measurement (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM), empty when the paper does not give one

date_basis.description: Where the date comes from (text or a figure caption)

metric.description: Spatial average, interior, LEQ16 (16-hour work period equivalent level), LEQ8 (8-hour sleep period)

sound_level_dba.description: A-weighted sound level (UCUM has no A-weighting; the weighting is A)

quote.description: The sentence the numbers come from, verbatim apart from words the PDF hyphenates across line ends

preprocessing: Hand-picked statements written as rows by build_iss_acoustic_levels.py in this folder; the script checks every quote against the PDF text layer (pdftotext from poppler, raw mode) and stops if one is missing. Only numbers stated in the text are used; no value was read from a figure.
license: US Government work. NASA material is generally not subject to copyright in the United States (NASA media usage guidelines, https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/). Credit NASA as the source; no NASA logo or insignia is used (NASA-SOURCES.md section 4).
provenance_note: REPLAY of published NASA survey values with their measurement dates.
is_not: Summary values, not a sound level time series.
Area surveys are not a person's noise dose; only the LEQ16 and LEQ8 rows come from crew-worn dosimeters, and the paper's group rows are averages over many sessions.

consumers.use: Per-area nominal levels for the SIM noise generator: work modules 46.2 to 67.4 dBA, sleep stations 43.8 to 59.2 dBA.

Golden inputs with NASA's own reading: sleep stations above 50 dBA (the sleep level in Flight Rule B13-152, as quoted) but below 62 dBA (hearing rest); the April 2020 LEQ16 of 73.0 dBA, above the 72 dBA limit, after which 'this crewmember was required to don HPD' (N33 p. 4).
Noise exposure scenario with a documented crew action (hearing protection).
